findings.title: Test never verifies frame was refused; try/catch passes either way
findings.claim: The try/catch(closed_error) block passes whether or not closed_error is thrown, so a regression where send() silently drops the frame or completes without calling put() would still pass the test; a BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW/BOOST_CHECK_EXCEPTION on closed_error would state the contract.

findings.title: Server-side hook path is untested
findings.claim: The server's stream connection gets the same hook via connection::send() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:1103) but server_factory.hooks is filled and never fired, so only the client side of the window is exercised; risk is small since the fix is in shared connection::send().

findings.title: Test won't compile below API level 9
findings.claim: put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>) only exists when SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9, but CMake still lists 7 as a selectable value; tls_test.cc guards the same override with #if while this test and output_stream_test.cc don't, though no CI job builds at an old level so it's minor.

findings.title: Doc overstates when the connection shuts down
findings.claim: The statement "The stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed" contradicts line 49 of the same file, which says closing the client aborts the stream; a connection error or server stop also shuts it down. The same wording issue appears in the sink doxygen at include/seastar/rpc/rpc_types.hh:339-342. Suggested fix: "...is shut down normally once both halves are closed".

findings.title: Code comment slightly inaccurate about who waits on _outgoing_queue_ready
findings.claim: The comment "Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on" isn't quite true because stop_send_loop() still does when_all(std::move(_outgoing_queue_ready), ...); it now gets the ready future via std::exchange, and the real drain is observed through _sink_closed_future. The comment should say that.

findings.title: const_cast used to mutate hooks from a const override
findings.claim: The test factory uses const_cast to mutate hooks from a const override; declaring hooks as mutable would be cleaner.

findings.title: PR description ends with Claude Code attribution line
findings.claim: The PR body ends with "🤖 Generated with Claude Code", which the user's global rules say must never appear.

findings.title: Issue references resolve against the wrong repo in the fork
findings.claim: "Fixes #3663" / "Refs #3653" are upstream Seastar issue numbers, but in dkropachev/ironweave they resolve against this repo, and "Fixes" would auto-close whatever issue #3663 is here on merge.

findings.title: PR description links internal Jira tickets
findings.claim: The PR body links internal CUSTOMER-* Jira tickets.
